state.bunkers-text: Bunkers on board at commencement and at completion of each port operation are recorded in the joint statement of facts and are settled between the parties on the quantities so recorded at the price stated in the charter.

criteria.false: The span from the outage start to the status time is four hours or less.

q3.instructions: Which next step fits the transmitter outage at the status time?

criteria.switch_to_standby_feed: Move programme output onto the tested standby chain now.
criteria.send_engineer_first: Dispatch a repair engineer to the relay before changing the feed.
criteria.retry_remote_reset: Make another remote reset attempt on the main exciter.
criteria.seek_licence_extension: Ask the regulator for a longer outage allowance and keep the main chain down for repair.

q4.instructions: Count the scheduled programme slots that did not air at all during the outage, considering only slots whose start time is on or after the moment the site went off air and on or before the status time recorded in the state. A slot whose start time falls after the status time is excluded even if it is listed as not aired. A slot that was aired as a rerun counts as aired and is not counted. Rate the resulting count.
criteria: Many: 6 or more slots not aired

q5.instructions: The standby chain passed its last test less than seven days before the outage began.

criteria.true: The last test date and time falls within the seven days before the outage start.
criteria.false: The last test date and time falls earlier than seven days before the outage start.

q6.instructions: Which external notification step is due at the status time?

criteria.notify_regulator_now: Send the regulator the outage notice the licence requires once the notice threshold has been passed.
criteria.publish_listener_notice_only: Post an on-air and web notice to listeners without contacting the regulator.
criteria.wait_until_restored: Hold all external notices until the feed is back on air.

PART 1. PROCEDURE CDS-4.2 (ISSUE 2), EXTRACT
1.1 Scope. This procedure covers every chilled and blast-chilled area on site. An excursion is a period during which a probe reads above 5.0°C.
1.2 Duration. The duration of an excursion runs from the first above-limit reading of the period to the first reading at or below 5.0°C that follows it.
1.3 Merging. If a probe reads above 5.0°C again within 20 minutes of an earlier return to 5.0°C or below, the two periods form one excursion. Its duration runs from the first above-limit reading of the first period to the first reading at or below 5.0°C after the last above-limit reading of the merged run.
1.4 Routes, by duration and peak:
(a) 30 minutes or less, with a peak at or below 7.0°C: internal log entry only, no notice to the Board.
(b) More than 30 minutes and up to 120 minutes, or 30 minutes or less with a peak above 7.0°C: written notice to the Board within 5 working days of discovery.
(c) More than 120 minutes: same-day telephone notice to the Board duty line, followed by written notice within 5 working days of discovery.
1.5 Working days. Monday to Friday, excluding the public holidays listed in Annex B. The day of discovery is not counted; the first working day after it is day 1.
1.6 Discovery. For the purpose of 1.5, discovery is the date on which the excursion is first entered in the site deviation log.
1.7 Sign-off. The site quality manager signs every notification to the Board.
1.8 Records. Every excursion, including one logged internally only, is kept on file for three years.

ANNEX A. GLOSSARY (ISSUE 2)
Discovery: the time at which an alarm for the excursion is acknowledged by a member of staff.
Peak: the highest reading recorded during an excursion.

Notice counts from the date the administrator logs it in the case log, not the date the member signs the form and not the date it was posted.

Rule 7.2 Early retirement reduction. Where a pension starts before the member's 65th birthday (normal pension age), it is reduced for each whole month between the pension start date and that birthday. The reduction is 0.25% per whole month, except that members who were in the legacy section on 31 December 2009 have a reduction of 0.20% per whole month. A whole month is counted each time one calendar month can be added to the pension start date without the resulting date passing the 65th birthday. Part months are ignored.

Rule 9.4 Career breaks. An unpaid approved career break counts as pensionable service at 50% for up to 24 months, provided written approval was given before the break began. Pensionable service is counted in whole calendar months.

Rule 10.1 Accrual. Pension accrues at 1/60 of final pensionable salary for each year of pensionable service. Final pensionable salary is the figure certified by the employer.

Rule 11.1 Cash option and partner consent. The cash option exchanges 25% of the pension for a lump sum. It is paid only if the partner's signed consent is logged by the administrator within 30 days after the pension start date. The receipt date is the date recorded in the case log when the original consent is first logged. The postmark date and any date written on the form do not count. The 30 days are calendar days counted after the pension start date. If valid consent is not logged in time, the cash option is not paid, the pension is paid without any exchange, and the early retirement itself may still go ahead.

Rule 12.2 Withdrawn illustrations. Any benefit illustration issued before a rule check or correction is withdrawn and must not be relied on.

state:
TELPORARA GROWERS TRUST - FROST PLANNING MEMO
Memo Reference: TGT-FP-2026-04-1187
Issued By: Tharten Feahurst, Planning Desk
Issued To: Jeackard Stuckhurst, Block Operations, Toport Depot
Issued On: 2026-04-14, 16:40
Subject: Night frost protection decision for Block B (pears), night of 2026-04-15

1. Background
Block B is a 6.2 ha pear planting in the Sendgate valley and is at full bloom this week. The crop value at risk for Block B this season is GBP 58,000. Block A (apples, 9.4 ha, off Kangate Street) is at an earlier bud stage, is not covered by this memo, and needs no decision today.
Weather station WS-4 logged a minimum of -0.6 C on 2026-04-13. This is for the file only.

2. Forecast Evidence
The 18:00 ensemble run has 40 members. Canopy-height air temperature is forecast to fall below the critical threshold of -2.5 C at any time before 07:00 on 2026-04-16 in 14 of the 40 members. A member at exactly -2.5 C is not below the threshold. Members that stay at or above the threshold, or only dip below it after 07:00, are not counted.
The earlier 06:00 run gave 22 of 40 members. It was superseded by the 18:00 run and must not be used for this decision.

3. Protection Options
Option W (wind machine hire): GBP 650 per night, including the operator. Trials at Nendfield County plots showed it prevents 60% of the loss a critical frost would otherwise cause.
Option H (fuel-fired heaters, 30 units): GBP 1,900 per night, including fuel and a standby technician. Trials showed it prevents 85% of the loss a critical frost would otherwise cause.
Each option can be run on its own. Combined operation has not been trialled and is outside this memo.

4. Decision Rule
The desk ranks options by expected loss prevented minus the nightly cost. Expected loss prevented = probability of critical frost x crop value at risk x share of loss prevented. The probability is the number of ensemble members below the threshold divided by the total number of members. The option with the highest result is the one to run. Running nothing has a result of zero.

5. Other Items (not for this decision)
- The Block A pruning contractor invoice of GBP 3,260 remains with Haindus Grellock for review.
- The Block C irrigation pump service is booked for 2026-05-02 at Sendgate Depot.
- Froumel Thafield Ltd has asked whether the Toport Depot store can take spare fuel drums; no reply yet.

6. Action
Block Operations to confirm the chosen option to the Planning Desk by 17:30 today.

LP-7.1 Annual cap. No premises may host temporary events on more than 21 event days in any calendar year. The cap belongs to the premises and does not follow the licence holder to other premises.

LP-7.2 Year attribution. An event day is counted in the calendar year in which that day falls. Event days falling in another calendar year are not counted against the current year, even if the notice was received in the current year.

LP-7.3 Counting. Each notified event day counts once. Counting starts from the date the Board receives the notice. For a notice delivered by post this is the date on the Board's receipt stamp; for a notice lodged online it is the portal receipt date. The date written on a paper or PDF form is not used for this purpose. A notified day stops counting only if the holder withdraws that day in writing before the first day of the event on that date. A withdrawal removes only the days it names. A variation that adds event days counts the added days in full from the date the variation is received.

LP-7.4 Notice period. A notice is on the standard route if it is received at least 28 clear days before the first event day. Clear days exclude both the day of receipt and the first event day. Any notice received with fewer clear days is a late notice and must be referred to the Board for decision at its next sitting.

LP-7.5 Fees. The 2026 day fee is £46 for each event day notified. A late notice carries a flat surcharge of £60 in addition to the day fee. No surcharge applies to a notice on the standard route.

LP-7.6 Overlapping days. Where two notices name the same calendar day at the same premises, that day is counted once.

LP-7.7 Other premises. Each premises has its own annual cap. Event days at a different premises do not count, even where the same holder is named on both notices.

LP-7.8 Decisions. The Board records its decisions in the minutes. A decision on a notice, including a decision to refer or to defer, does not change the count under LP-7.3 unless the holder has withdrawn days in writing as LP-7.3 provides.

LP-7.9 Records. Holders must keep copies of every receipt and every written withdrawal. The Board may ask for these before issuing a fee notice.

LP-7.10 Review. The policy is reviewed each January. No change was agreed for the 2026 review.

LP-7.11 Appeals. A holder may appeal a refusal or a condition to the Board's appeal panel within 14 days of the written decision. An appeal does not stop a notice from being counted.

LP-7.12 Order of processing. Notices are processed in the order their receipt is recorded. Where a notice is received on the same day as another notice for the same premises, the notices are listed on the same agenda.

LP-7.13 Bulletin. Late notices are listed in the Board's monthly bulletin, together with the reason recorded by the officer. Listing in the bulletin does not itself change a notice's route.

scheme-rules-extract.rule-4-2: Pensionable service runs from the join date to the last day of pensionable employment, with both of those days included.
scheme-rules-extract.rule-4-3a: An unpaid absence of 30 consecutive days or fewer counts as pensionable service. An absence is consecutive when no paid day falls inside it.
scheme-rules-extract.rule-4-3b: An unpaid absence of more than 30 consecutive days is excluded from pensionable service unless the trustees approve it in writing. The trustees may give that approval at any time, and an approved absence then counts as pensionable service.
scheme-rules-extract.rule-4-4: One year of pensionable service is 365 days. Adjusted service is the number of days from the join date to the last day of pensionable employment, both included, less the days of any excluded absence. Complete years are the whole number of 365-day periods in adjusted service.
scheme-rules-extract.rule-5-1: Benefits are paid monthly in arrears on the last working day of the month.
scheme-rules-extract.rule-6-1: The early retirement reduction band is set by the member's age in whole years on the pension start date stated in the most recent retirement election received.
scheme-rules-extract.rule-6-2: A retirement election must be received at least 30 days before its pension start date. Days are counted from the day after receipt up to and including the pension start date.
scheme-rules-extract.rule-6-3: Where an election is replaced by a later election, only the later election is used for the start date and the reduction band.

Policies.Title: Working day definition
Policies.Text: A working day is any day from Monday to Friday that does not appear in the site closure calendar. When counting working days from an event, the day of the event is not counted and the first working day after it is day 1. A submission counts as made on the date the regulator's portal records its receipt.

Policies.Title: External reporting of stock differences
Policies.Text: Any unexplained difference between the register balance and the physical count of a Schedule 2 product must be reported to the Hertholm Medicines Inspectorate within three working days of the day the difference was discovered. A difference is explained when a documented entry, such as a dispensing record or a witnessed destruction log, accounts for it. Explained differences are recorded as register corrections and do not, on their own, require a report.

Policies.Title: Schedule 3 differences
Policies.Text: An unexplained difference of one unit or fewer on a Schedule 3 product is recorded in an internal note to the Responsible Pharmacist. An explained difference on a Schedule 3 product requires only a register correction with the documentary reference.

Policy Extract.Title: Mature and Returning Learners Route: eligibility and document rules
Clauses: C1: An applicant who holds a Level 3 or higher qualification is not eligible for this route.
C2: Qualifying experience is counted only from approved fields: environmental monitoring, surveying, hydrology or land management. Other employment is not counted.

C3: Qualifying experience is counted only within the most recent unbroken span. A span is a run of approved employment spells in which no gap between consecutive spells is longer than 30 consecutive days. A gap of 30 days or fewer does not end a span, and the gap days themselves are not counted as experience.
C4: Days in a spell are counted inclusively, from the first day to the last day. The total qualifying days are divided by 365 and rounded down to give full years of qualifying experience.

C5: Five or more full years: direct offer without interview. Three or four full years: interview required before any offer. Fewer than three full years: not eligible for this route; standard entry only.
C6: The employer reference must be signed by the applicant's line manager, or by a more senior manager with direct oversight of the applicant's role.

C7: Supporting documents must be received within 21 calendar days after the application submission date. The submission date is not counted. A document is treated as received on the date of the first upload that opens as a readable file.

C8: An application fee waiver covers an application if the application is submitted on or before the waiver's last valid date. The last valid date is 60 calendar days after the issue date, with the issue date not counted.
C9: Where an office notice extends fee waivers, the extended last valid date replaces the original last valid date for every waiver within the notice's scope.

rules.cover_trigger: The weather cover pays when the gauge records 5.0 mm or more on the shoot date.
rules.decision_rule: Compare expected costs. Expected cost of a date = (years stopped / years observed) * full_day_lost_if_stopped. Moving adds the move fee plus the expected cost of the backup date. Insurance recovery is ignored.

=== B. SCHEME RULES (EXTRACT) ===
1.1 Retirement date means the date from which the pension is first payable.
1.2 Complete year means a full twelve-month period counted forward from the retirement date.
1.3 Calendar months are counted back from a date on the same day of the month; where that day does not exist in the earlier month, the last day of that month applies.
2.1 Pensionable service is counted in whole months from the date of joining the scheme.
2.2 Service records that are added late are backdated to the date of joining and are reflected in the next revaluation certificate.
3.1 Normal pension age (NPA) is the member's 65th birthday.
3.2 A member may retire early from age 55 by giving written notice. The notice must be given at least three calendar months before the proposed retirement date. Where notice arrives by post, the date of receipt is the date stamped by the Nolfell post room, not the date the notice is later logged or scanned into the case system.
3.3 An early pension is reduced from the accrued pension at NPA by 4% for each complete year between the retirement date and NPA. Part years are disregarded.
3.4 Where a member retires before age 60, the trustees must consent before the pension starts. From age 60 onward no trustee consent is needed.
3.5 The accrued pension at NPA used in any calculation is the figure on the most recent revaluation certificate issued by the administrator. A later certificate replaces an earlier one in full.
4.1 Transfers out of the scheme are dealt with under rule 4 and are not covered in this pack.
5.1 Benefits are paid subject to the tax rules in force at the time. The administrator does not give tax advice.
6.1 On death in service the scheme pays a lump sum of four times pensionable salary, within 60 days of notification.
7.1 Pensions in payment are increased each April at the rate set by the trustees.

An extension of that deadline takes effect only when an Admissions Officer records a written approval in the activity log, and the extension applies only to the applicant named in the approval.

Evidence is late when it is received after the effective evidence deadline. Late evidence received no more than 5 working days after the effective deadline is referred to the Admissions Panel, which decides whether to reinstate the offer. Evidence received more than 5 working days after the effective deadline lapses the offer without referral.
A working day is any Monday to Friday that is not listed in the Closure Calendar. When counting working days between two dates, the earlier date is not counted and the later date is counted.
Receipt is the date the evidence is logged as received by the Admissions Office. The date on which the sender posted or emailed the evidence does not count as the receipt date.
The number of calendar days late is the number of calendar days from the effective evidence deadline to the receipt date.
Where an examination remark changes a grade, the certificate showing the remarked grade is the evidence that counts for the condition.

Clauses.Exceedance: A compliance sample result above the permit limit for the parameter at the sampled outfall, using the limit in force on the sample date. A result voided by the laboratory is not an exceedance and is left out of every count.
Clauses.Significant_Exceedance: An exceedance whose result is more than 25 per cent above the limit in force on the sample date.
Clauses.Notification_Rule: Each significant exceedance must be notified to the agency. Other exceedances are entered in the internal log and summarised in the monthly return.
Clauses.Notification_Deadline: A significant exceedance must be notified within the number of working days set by the amendment in force on the sample date, counted from the sample date. The sample date is not counted. Saturdays, Sundays, public holidays and site closure days are not working days.
Clauses.Confirmation_Sample: After a significant exceedance a confirmation sample is taken within 1 working day of the sample date, counted in the same way. If the confirmation result is at or below the limit in force on its own sample date, routine sampling resumes. If it is above that limit, enhanced weekly sampling starts.
Clauses.Monthly_Count: Exceedances for a calendar month are counted by sample date, outfall by outfall, using the limit in force on each sample date. Results from other outfalls are counted only against their own limits.

2. riskAssessmentAction
The fire risk assessment dated 2026-08-20 (ref FRA-WA-2026-03) lists this door as action FRA-07. The stated completionDeadline for FRA-07 is 2026-09-12. The assessor set that date and the trust has not extended it.

3. interimControlsTried
- 2026-08-28: caretaker fitted a rubber doorstop to hold the door open. Not accepted: a propped fire door is not an interim control under trust procedure FSP-3.
- 2026-09-02: door found wedged open at 08:15; the doorstop had been moved.
- Head's note dated 2026-09-03: a fire door that cannot be seen to close fully is not a control. The corridor may be used only while the door closes fully on its own.

4. peopleRecorded
Six Year 8 and Year 9 science forms walk the corridor to the labs, with 28 pupils on each form register. Four teachers walk the same corridor to those rooms on every school day. The whole-school roll is 1,140 pupils, but only the groups above are recorded as using this corridor.

Thoupanara Fire Systems Ltd (Unit 4, Panness Trading Estate) quote TFS-Q-88310, dated 2026-09-04: replacement closer arm and adjustment at £1,260.00 net, plus VAT at 20%. Earliest booked visit: 2026-09-16.
Trust purchasing rule PR-12: a quote whose total including VAT exceeds £1,500.00 needs a second quote before any order is placed.

6. closureRule
Trust procedure FSP-7: a defect on a fire door is closed only after a functional test signed by the trust fire safety adviser. The estates manager and the contractor may record completed works, but neither can close the defect.

Sports hall emergency lighting: three of 22 luminaires failed the 2026-08-31 test. Replacement invoice £380.00 sits on separate work order WO-2291, which does not relate to FD-14.

excursion-procedure.reading-classes: A warm reading is any logged temperature greater than the alarm threshold, that is, less negative than -65. A compliant reading is any logged temperature at or below the alarm threshold.
excursion-procedure.excursion-definition: A run of consecutive warm readings forms one excursion. The excursion starts at the first warm reading of the run and ends at the first compliant reading after the run. Its duration is the clock time from the start to the end. Any compliant reading ends a run, and there is no merging tolerance for short compliant gaps.
excursion-procedure.reference-logger: The primary logger of the unit is the reference for every timestamp unless a later written instruction from the Quality Officer names a different reference logger for a specific timestamp on a specific unit.
excursion-procedure.deviation-rule: A single excursion longer than 30 minutes requires a deviation report to the Quality Officer, filed within 2 calendar days after the excursion ends. An excursion of 30 minutes or less is recorded in the monthly summary only.
excursion-procedure.daily-total-rule: Excursion minutes are summed across all excursions on one unit that start on the same calendar day. If that total is more than 60 minutes, the unit contents are quarantined pending stability review.

backup-readings.note: Backup logger readings are kept for comparison. They do not replace primary readings unless a written instruction names them for a specific timestamp.

From: Railus Clackstead, Network Planning, Ruswirtex Grid Services Ltd
To: Clesin Kafertwick, Asset Management
Site: Hamgate Primary Substation, transformer TX-2 (feeder F-37)

Purpose
This memo summarises the emergency-rating exceedance record for TX-2 and sets out the options for the next 30-day window. Only emergency-rating exceedances are treated as trip events here.

Exceedance record
Comparable 30-day windows were selected from last year by matching forecast peak temperature and forecast feeder demand. The next window is forecast to match that profile, and no change to the feeder configuration is planned before it starts. Ten comparable windows were reviewed. In seven of them, at least one exceedance occurred. In the other three, none occurred.
The annual log separately records 6 exceedance events in 2025 across all months. This is an events-per-year count and is not a probability for any single window.

Cost inputs
trip_cost_gbp: 90000 (charged once per window in which at least one exceedance occurs; covers unserved energy and emergency repair)
transfer_charge_gbp: 18000 (fixed; moves feeder load to Waismouth Feeder F-41 for the whole window)
monitoring_charge_gbp: 0 (alarms already installed)
transfer_removes_exposure: yes, for the whole window, provided F-41 stays within its own rating

Other items
- TX-1 at Hamgate was refurbished in 2024; oil sample results sit in appendix B, not reviewed here.
- Meter batch 0417 has 212 estimated reads, unrelated to this review.
- Fleet van VN-882 service due 2026-06-01.
- Gandard Thunpertton has a query on the tap-changer log; reply pending.
- Contact: r.clackstead@ruswirtex-grid.example

criteria.false: The share of comparable windows with at least one exceedance is 50 percent or less.

q2.instructions: Which course of action has the lower expected total cost over the next 30-day window?

criteria.pre_emptive_transfer: Pay the fixed transfer charge and move the feeder load for the whole window, so no trip cost arises in that window.
criteria.monitoring_only: Pay no charge and accept the expected trip cost implied by the comparable-window record.
criteria.other: Some other course of action, or a combination of the options above.

request.text: Confirm the total added time for this match from the stoppage log. Give the total in whole minutes, list every counted stoppage with its duration in seconds, and name each logged entry left out with the reason. Apply added_time_rule only.

added_time_rule.basis: Sum the durations of all stoppages marked counted true, across both halves, in seconds.
added_time_rule.rounding: Round the sum once to the nearest whole minute: 30 seconds or more rounds up, under 30 seconds rounds down. Do not round each half separately.
added_time_rule.excluded: Entries marked counted false are not match stoppages and are not summed.

criteria.false: The stated total differs from the result of applying the summing and rounding rules to the entries marked counted true.

criteria.excluded_entry_added: An entry marked not counted was included in the sum.

policy.title: Cold-storage excursion counting and integrity checks
rules: R1. An excursion is a period in which the unit records a temperature above the alarm threshold, measured from the first reading above the threshold to the first reading back at or below it.
R2. Where a recorder download covers the event, the times in that download are the authority and replace the times in the excursion log.
R3. Only excursions in the unit where the batch is stored count toward the batch. An excursion shorter than 5 minutes does not count.
R4. An excursion that starts and ends inside an approved facilities service window for that unit does not count.
R5. Each counted excursion needs an integrity check of batch samples recorded no later than 48 hours after the excursion's end time. Excursions that do not count need no check.
R6. If any counted excursion lacks a check recorded inside that 48-hour window, the batch is placed on quality hold until the QA lead signs a release.
R7. A quality hold is lifted only by a written waiver signed by the QA lead. A waiver signed by any other role is void, and the batch status must follow the hold.

DEFINITIONS
Calendar day: every day counted, including weekends and public holidays.
Cleared: a payment counts as cleared on the day the board's bank feed shows the funds received.

RP-4 Renewal windows
(a) The receipt date of a renewal is the later of: the date the application first reaches complete status on the portal, and the date the renewal fee payment is cleared. Complete status means every required document is attached and the declaration has been submitted.
(b) A renewal received on or before the licence expiry date pays the standard renewal fee only.
(c) A renewal received after the expiry date and no later than the 14th calendar day after the expiry date pays the standard renewal fee plus the late surcharge. The 14th calendar day after expiry is inside the window.
(d) A renewal received after the 14th calendar day after expiry lapses, and a new application is required.
(e) A renewal received under (b) or (c) continues the licence without a gap, starting on the day after the previous expiry date. This applies whether or not a surcharge is payable.
(f) Administrative charges, such as duplicate certificates, are not renewal fees and are not part of the renewal payment.

OP-7 Portal outage relief
(a) Where the first failed payment attempt for a renewal falls on a day inside a logged portal outage, the late surcharge is waived, provided the successful payment is cleared no later than three calendar days after the logged outage ends.
(b) Relief under OP-7 removes the late surcharge only. It does not change the receipt date determined under RP-4(a).

RP-9 Change of trading name
A change of trading name must be notified within 28 calendar days. Notification fee: 40.00 GBP. Not connected to renewal.

The Premises_Log and Supply_Orders were checked for context and are not part of the royalty timing record.

Agreement.Territory_Note: Exclusive trading area within 2 km of each outlet

Key_Clauses.Clause_6_Royalty_Rate: Royalty is 6 per cent of Net Sales for each calendar month and is due on the 15th calendar day of the following month.
Key_Clauses.Clause_6_Payment_Date: A payment is made on its value date, meaning the date cleared funds are credited to the Franchisor's bank account. The date on which the Franchisee sends a transfer is not the payment date.
Key_Clauses.Clause_6_Monthly_Statement: A monthly statement of Net Sales must be filed by the 7th calendar day of the following month. A late statement does not move the royalty due date.
Key_Clauses.Clause_6_Brand_Levy: A brand levy of 2 per cent of Net Sales is payable to the marketing fund on the same due date as the royalty and is not part of the royalty.
Key_Clauses.Clause_9_Grace_Window: Counting the due date as day zero, a royalty payment whose value date falls on or before the last day of the grace window is within grace. A value date after the last day of the window makes the payment a Late Royalty Payment. The grace window is 5 calendar days unless an amendment states otherwise.
Key_Clauses.Clause_9_4_Late_Charge: Overdue royalty bears a late charge of 4 per cent per annum from the due date until paid. The late charge is separate from royalty and from any audit adjustment.
Key_Clauses.Clause_11_Audit: The Franchisor may audit Net Sales. Net Sales found by audit to exceed reported Net Sales are payable at the Clause 6 rate, with the adjustment payable within 30 days of the audit report.
Key_Clauses.Clause_14_1_Default_Notice: For a Late Royalty Payment not waived in writing, the Franchisor may serve a Default Notice. The Franchisee has a Cure Period of 10 Business Days after receipt of the notice to cure the default.
Key_Clauses.Clause_14_3_Persistent_Late_Payment: Notwithstanding Clause 14.1, if three or more Late Royalty Payments occur in any rolling twelve-month period, the Franchisor may terminate this Agreement by written notice with immediate effect and without any Cure Period. A rolling twelve-month period is the twelve months ending on the date of the Franchisor's review, and each payment is placed in that period by its due date. A payment the Franchisor has waived in writing for all purposes of this Agreement is not counted.
Key_Clauses.Business_Day: A day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday.

Amendments.Summary: Revised trading hours schedule for the Thencombe Market Outlet. No change to royalty or grace terms.

FISHERIES BYCATCH ALLOWANCE MEMO
Ref: KBT-BCR-0318 | Date: 3 March 2026
From: Froumia Clulworth, Fisheries Officer, Kargundex Marine Trust (f.clulworth@kargundex-marine.org)
To: Toulus Rinby, Secretary, Licensing Panel
Subject: Juvenile cod bycatch on vessel KV-4471, demersal permit review

1. Background
Vessel KV-4471 holds a demersal permit with a juvenile cod allowance of 2.0 per cent by weight of the sampled catch. The allowance is measured per sampling period, not per fishing hour.

2. Observed sampling
Three hauls were sampled by the observer on trip T-88 (ref 0912-b) out of Pisgate. Combined figures for the three hauls:
- Total sampled catch weight: 1,520 kg
- Juvenile cod weighed from the sample: 34.6 kg
- Fishing time covered by the three sampled hauls: 71.5 hours
Trip fuel spend (GBP 4,870) is not part of this review.

3. Season model
The assessor ran the season model 500 times using the sampling figures and the remaining planned trips. In 318 of the 500 runs the cod allowance was exceeded if the vessel continued fishing unchanged. The model does not allow for weather days.

4. Options costed by the assessor
(a) Observer cover on the next trips: fixed cover fee GBP 6,500. With cover in place, the assessor puts the chance of exceeding the allowance at 15 in 100.
(b) Close the fishing area to KV-4471 for 14 days: lost landings of GBP 2,300 per day. The closure stops fishing before the remaining trips, so the allowance cannot be exceeded this season.
(c) No change: the chance of exceeding the allowance is as given in section 3. If the allowance is exceeded, the penalty is GBP 60,000.
Costs under (a) and (b) are fixed and certain. The penalty under (c) is incurred only if the allowance is exceeded.

5. Other items
KV-4471 was inspected at Dreckgate on 19 January 2026 with no findings. Sister vessel KV-4490 has a separate review (ref KBT-BCR-0319). Panel meeting: 17 March 2026.

q1.instructions: How many overrun days are chargeable on this hire's late return under the overrun rule in the record? Apply the rule exactly as follows: the overrun clock starts at the scheduled return time minus the grace hours (the grace is deducted from the scheduled return time, not added after it). Measure the elapsed time from that start point to the actual return moment. Each 24-hour block of that elapsed time, or part of one, counts as one overrun day. MEMO

issued_by: Rondo Teamley, Unit Production Office, Norhemex Pictures Ltd
issued_to: Thirtia Dremwick, Line Producer
issued_on: 2026-06-08
subject: Night exterior, quarry road scene, Thortcombe

1. Purpose
This memo sets out where the quarry road night exterior (scene_ref 44B) should be shot. The outdoor shoot is scheduled for the night of 2026-07-14, the only night the lead cast can attend. A stoppage means the unit is sent to holding on the night because of rain; no other cause is counted in this memo.

2. Options under review
Option A (outdoor_no_cover): shoot on site on the scheduled night with no rain protection. No hire cost is added.
Option B (outdoor_with_cover): shoot on site with a rain cover rig hired at a fixed fee of GBP 18,400 for the shoot. The rig keeps the set workable through any rain that would otherwise cause a stoppage on the night. It changes no other cost.
Option C (move_to_stage): build the quarry set at Theanjenix Studios, Stage 3. Fixed cost is GBP 41,000 stage hire plus GBP 18,500 set rebuild.

3. Cost of a lost night
If a stoppage occurs, the unit's cost for that night is GBP 50,000, charged in full with no partial-day recovery. The figure covers crew, cast standby and equipment.

4. Weather evidence
The long-range forecast issued 2026-06-05 gives no reliable signal for the night of 2026-07-14, so the decision rests on past seasons. Production logs show 40 outdoor night calls in the same two-week window over the past ten seasons. On 12 of those 40 calls, recorded rain exceeded the stoppage threshold and the unit was sent to holding. The other 28 calls ran to completion. Rain gauge readings at the Mailhaven station averaged 2.1 mm per hour across all 40 calls and are given for reference only.

5. Location owner terms
The quarry is leased from Thunjabrook Estates at a location fee of GBP 12,000. A cancellation confirmed more than 28 full days before the shoot date carries no charge. A cancellation confirmed 28 full days before the shoot date or less carries a charge of half the location fee.

6. Other items (not part of this decision)
Crew call on the night is 16:00 and the unit vehicle count is 14. Insurance excess is GBP 2,500 and applies to claims only, not to stoppages. A generator upgrade quote requested by the gaffer is still pending.

Contact: rulldale.ops@norhemex-pictures.example

domain: regional airline turboprop bleed valve deferral and standby aircraft swaps
state:
MEMO FRM-OPS-2026-0319
From: Grinen Joundale, Technical Records Lead, Frumairon Regional Air
To: Poundin Cison, Duty Operations Controller
Date: 2026-03-19
Subject: Tail FR-TP-204 bleed valve fault and Friday rotation

Background
Tail FR-TP-204 reported an intermittent bleed valve fault (ATA 36-11) on the sector Winness to Doullfell on 2026-03-16. The valve was reset on the ground, no engine shutdown occurred, and the aircraft was released to service. The valve has not been replaced. The fault is logged as a repeat-type defect in the reliability database.

Reliability method
The reliability board agreed the following method in January. It is restated here so the figures can be checked.
- Per-sector figure = recorded events on the same fault code ÷ sectors flown.
- Use the tail's own history where it has flown at least 1,000 sectors since its last valve overhaul. Otherwise use the fleet-wide figure for the type.
- Chance of at least one event across n planned sectors = n × per-sector figure. The shortcut is used because per-sector figures are small.
- Expected cost of an option = chance of at least one event across the rotation × all-in cost of one in-flight event. An option with no event risk has an expected cost equal to its fixed cost.

Tail history
FR-TP-204 has flown 1,250 sectors since its valve overhaul on 2025-11-04 and has recorded 2 events on this fault code in that time. Fleet-wide, the type has recorded 3 events in 15,000 sectors on the same code; this figure is shown for information only. FR-TP-199 has a separate cabin fan fault (ATA 21-30) with 4 events in 2,000 sectors, which does not bear on the valve.

Friday rotation
FR-TP-204 is planned for four sectors on Friday 2026-03-20: Doullfell to Ceanness, Ceanness to Winness, Winness to Doullfell, and Doullfell to Ceanness.

Costs (from Finance, ref FIN-41-07)
- All-in cost of one in-flight event, including diversion, rebooking and passenger care: £600,000.
- Swap to standby tail FR-TP-207 (valve overhauled 2026-01-12): fixed cost £3,150 for crew positioning and ferry. For this comparison the standby tail is treated as carrying no event risk.
- Ground FR-TP-204 for the day to replace the valve: £22,400 of lost flying.

Other items, not relevant to this decision: cabin seat fabric order PO-8812 (£4,980); crew recurrent training moved to 2026-04-07; catering invoice reference Ceanness-0334 pending approval.

Poundin, please confirm the option by 16:00 today so the rotation can be planned. Technical Records will sign off whichever option is chosen.

q1.instructions: Using the stated method and the tail's own history, the chance that the bleed valve fault recurs on at least one of the four Friday sectors is below one in a thousand.

criteria.true: The chance computed by the stated method is under 0.1%.
criteria.false: The chance computed by the stated method is 0.1% or more.

q2.instructions: Under the stated expected-cost method, which option has the lowest expected cost for the Friday rotation?

criteria.dispatch_as_planned: Operate all four sectors with the aircraft as scheduled, carrying the expected cost of an in-flight event.
criteria.swap_to_standby: Fly the rotation with the standby tail instead, carrying only its fixed cost.
criteria.ground_for_repair: Take the aircraft out of service for the day to replace the valve, carrying only its lost-flying cost.

q3.instructions: Rate the likelihood that the bleed valve fault recurs on any one given sector of this tail, using the per-sector figure from the stated method.
criteria: low: 0.05% up to under 0.5% per sector
moderate: 0.5% up to under 5% per sector

check.q1: Tail's own history: 1,250 sectors (at least 1,000, so used) with 2 events -> 2 ÷ 1,250 = 0.0016 per sector; 4 × 0.0016 = 0.0064 = 0.64%; 0.64% is not under 0.10% -> false
check.q2: Dispatch: 4 × 0.0016 = 0.0064; 0.0064 × £600,000 = £3,840. Swap: fixed £3,150 (no event risk). Ground: fixed £22,400. Lowest is 3,150 < 3,840 < 22,400 -> swap_to_standby
check.q3: Tail's own history: 2 events ÷ 1,250 sectors = 0.0016 = 0.16% per sector; 0.05% ≤ 0.16% < 0.5% -> band 'low' (index 1)

policy_wording.clause_3_notification: The insured must notify the insurer of a loss within 30 calendar days after the date of loss. Counting starts on the day after the date of loss. policy_wording.clause_5_settlement_basis: An item bought less than 5 years before the date of loss is settled at replacement cost, meaning the replacement_gbp shown for the item as later revised in writing by the assessor. An item bought 5 years or more before the date of loss is settled at actual cash value, meaning the acv_gbp shown for the item. policy_wording.clause_6_jewellery_and_watches_limit: Amounts payable for unscheduled items in the jewellery and watches category are limited to 1,500 pounds per claim. Scheduled items in that category are not counted towards this limit.

policy_wording.clause_9_high_value_schedule: An item on the high-value schedule as in force on the date of loss is settled at the agreed replacement value shown on the schedule, whatever its age. A proposed schedule addition is not in force until the insurer has issued an endorsement adding it.

SECTION A - PROCEDURE EXTRACT (SRL-CM-07 rev 4)
A1 Scope. This extract sets how corrective evidence under an improvement notice is due, received, graded and closed. Where a written variation under A7 names an item, it prevails over A4 for that item only.
A2 Business day. A business day is any Monday to Friday that is not listed in Annex B. Annex B is the complete list of non-business weekdays for this procedure. Weekends are never business days.
A3 Counting. For any period stated in business days, the day on which the triggering event is received is not counted. Counting starts on the following day. The last day of the period is counted if it is a business day.
A4 Due date. Corrective evidence for each item is due within 20 business days of the notice receipt date, unless a written variation for that item is issued under A7.
A5 Grace. Evidence received after the due date in force, but no more than 3 business days after it, is logged as a minor lapse (grade L). Evidence received more than 3 business days after the due date in force is logged as a breach (grade B).
A6 Breach reporting. A grade B item must be reported to the regulator in writing within 2 business days of being logged as grade B. A grade L item is recorded on the file only and does not need a regulator report.
A7 Variation. A variation changes the due date of one named item only. It must be in writing from the regulator officer, quote the file ref, state the number of business days added and the date from which they are counted. A telephone agreement is not valid until confirmed in writing.
A8 Closure. A file may be closed only when every item has been received and graded. Closure must be countersigned by the Head of Compliance. If the Head of Compliance is absent on the closure request date, the Deputy Head of Compliance countersigns instead. Absence is taken from the company leave calendar.
A9 Record keeping. Each receipt, variation, call and countersignature is entered on the file control sheet on the date it happened.
A10 Fees. Regulator administrative fees are payable within 14 days of invoice and are recorded on the control sheet. Fees do not change any due date or grade under this extract.

=== A. SOP EXTRACT: SOP-ADM-07 v3.1, essential document filing into the trial master file (TMF) ===
4.1 Each ethics approval of a protocol amendment, together with the amended protocol and any amended site-facing documents, must be filed into the site TMF within the period set by 4.2 or 4.3.
4.2 Standard period: 10 working days, counted from the date of the ethics approval letter.
4.3 Extended period: 15 working days, counted in the same way, applies where the amendment changes the participant information sheet (PIS) or the consent form, or adds either of them.
4.4 Working day: a Monday to Friday that is not a site closure day listed in Appendix B. The approval date is day 0. The first counted day is the next calendar day, and each later working day is counted once in turn. Weekends and closure days are never counted. The deadline is the last counted working day of the period. A filing made on the deadline is on time.
4.5 A written notice from the sponsor or the monitor that names an amendment and states which period applies to it overrides 4.2 and 4.3 for that amendment. The coordinator records the notice in the filing log remarks.
4.6 Where more than one written notice is received for the same amendment, the most recent notice applies.
4.7 The filing date is the date the file is marked as filed in the TMF index, and it is entered in the filing log on the day of filing.
5.1 The filing log holds one line per ethics approval, recording the approval date, the filing date and the filer.
5.2 Filing confirmations are kept in Binder 3 at the site and retained for 15 years after study close.
5.3 Each deviation log entry is countersigned by the Principal Investigator within 3 calendar days of the entry being made.

Appendix B: Site closure days (not working days)
2026-01-01 New Year closure
2026-03-19 Staff development day, Tondmouth site
2026-04-03 Building maintenance
2026-05-25 Spring bank holiday closure

Appendix C: Deviation classes for late filing
C1: filed 1 to 5 working days after the applicable deadline: minor administrative deviation, logged on the site deviation log. No sponsor report is needed.
C2: filed more than 5 working days after the applicable deadline: major administrative deviation, notified to the sponsor within 2 working days of the filing.
C3: filed on or before the applicable deadline: no deviation is recorded.

Appendix D: Filing checklist (Annex 1 to SOP-ADM-07)
1. Confirm the ethics approval letter is signed and dated by the panel office.
2. Check that the protocol version number matches the version named in the letter.
3. Confirm which period applies under 4.2, 4.3 and any notice under 4.5 and 4.6, and record the basis in the filing log remarks.
4. Scan documents at 300 dpi, save as PDF, and name each file by amendment and version.
5. Enter the filing date in the filing log on the day of filing.

Appendix E: Glossary
TMF = trial master file. EDC = electronic data capture. PIS = participant information sheet. IP = investigational product.

--- POLICY EXTRACT RP-SC-03 (rev 3) ---
1. Retention. Samples are retained for 36 months counted from the collection date. Samples may be disposed of only after the retention period has ended, and subject to clauses 2 to 6.
2. Excursions. An excursion is a period in which a storage unit reads warmer than -65C. Each excursion is a separate event. The counted time for an event is the time logged against it. Counted times for the events affecting a batch's storage unit are added together. An event logged at under 10 minutes is disregarded.
3. Quarantine. Where the counted excursion total for a batch's storage unit is 240 minutes or more, the batch is placed on quarantine hold and must not be disposed of while the hold stands.
4. Hold release. A quarantine hold is lifted only by written sign-off from the chair of the Deviation Review Panel, and only after the linked deviation has been closed.
5. Approvals. Disposal of a batch that is not on hold requires sign-off from the principal investigator and the biosafety officer.
6. Notice. A disposal request must be submitted at least 10 working days before the scheduled disposal date. Working days are Monday to Friday, excluding published closure days. The day of submission is not counted; the scheduled disposal day is counted.

state:
MEMO FGZ-TX-0417
Date: 14 May 2026
From: Penan Froundstead, Asset Planning, Frellthorpe Grid Ltd
To: Stelon Bolson, Network Operations
Subject: T2 transformer, Doummouth Road substation, 90-day risk screen

1. Background
Unit T2 (serial DRS-88213, 30 MVA) has shown rising acetylene since February. Oil results on file:
- 11 Feb 2026: acetylene 4 ppm, hydrogen 62 ppm
- 02 May 2026: acetylene 17 ppm, hydrogen 71 ppm
Loading is unchanged. T2 is the only 30 MVA unit on the 11 kV bus at Doummouth Road. A bus tie to Theaminster is available for 60 days.

2. Screening basis
The screen uses a constant forced-outage rate: 4 forced outages across 25 unit-years of matching-signature service. The rate is per unit-year, not a probability. The window is the 90 days after this memo. This memo uses a 365-day year. Probability of at least one outage in the window = 1 - exp(-expected outages), where expected outages = rate x window years.

3. Sourcing note
Procedure GRD-PM-4, section 3, asks that rates come from units of the same manufacturer as the unit screened. The fleet record does not show the manufacturer of the 4 outages or the 25 unit-years. T2's make is unconfirmed.

4. Costs (GBP)
Replace T2 with a new unit, installed and commissioned: 410,000. Replacement removes T2's forced-outage risk for the window.
Keep T2 in service with oil sampling for one quarter: 9,000.
Forced outage at Doummouth Road, including emergency switching and repair: 1,200,000.

5. DGA action rule (GRD-PM-4, section 6)
Applies to the most recent oil sample.
Acetylene below 10 ppm: routine quarterly sampling.
Acetylene from 10 ppm up to and including 35 ppm: resample within 30 days.
Acetylene above 35 ppm: remove from service for inspection.

6. Other items
Feeder 7 cable fault rate is unrelated to T2 and not used here.
Ticket SEP-2214 closed 09 April 2026.

Requested: a recommendation on T2 for the Monday review.

criteria.resample_within_30_days: Take a new oil sample within 30 days.

PART A. PROCEDURE EXTRACT (PROC-CA-3, corrective action and civil penalties)

A1. A corrective action period is 28 calendar days. Day 0 is the date the notice is served on the licence holder, and the period runs to day 28 counted from that date. Deadlines are fixed calendar dates. No roll-forward applies to weekends or public holidays.

A2. Evidence of remediation received on or before the deadline date is treated as on time. Evidence received after the deadline date is late for that finding.

A3. A case officer may extend a deadline by written notice issued before the deadline date. The notice states the number of extension days. A corrected notice for the same finding supersedes the earlier notice from the date the corrected notice is issued, and the corrected figures apply from that date.

A4. A late finding attracts a civil penalty of £750 per finding. On review, the case officer may reduce the amount. A reduction decision recorded in the penalty ledger replaces the amount stated in the original penalty notice.

A5. An extension request may be lodged through the licensing portal, by e-mail to the general inbox, or by e-mail to the case officer's named address. A request lodged through the general inbox is treated as lodged on the date the general inbox acknowledgement is issued. A portal request that failed during a service outage is treated as lodged on the date of the attempt only where the service desk has confirmed that outage in writing for the window concerned.

A6. Copies of case files are charged at the published rate. A copy charge is not a civil penalty and is not entered in the penalty ledger.

A7. The noticeServed date shown in Part B is the date of service recorded on the case, whichever method of service was used.

A8. A civil penalty notice may be challenged by written representations within 21 calendar days of its issue date. Representations do not suspend the payment date unless the case officer records a suspension in the penalty ledger.

rr7Withdrawal: a written withdrawal of an election takes effect on the day the administrator receives it. Any election received before that day then has no effect. A new election may be received after a withdrawal.

1.2 Clear days: the day on which the notice is received and the first day of the event are both excluded. Every calendar day strictly between them counts. Weekends and public holidays count in the same way as other days.

1.3 Each premises may have no more than 15 valid temporary event notices in a calendar year.

1.4 Each premises may have no more than 21 event days in a calendar year. A multi-day event counts one event day for each calendar day it covers. Only valid notices are counted.

1.5 A notice that is not valid under rule 1.1 is not counted toward the limits in rules 1.3 and 1.4. The Board has no power to accept a notice received inside the 10 clear day period.

1.6 A notice may be withdrawn in writing to the designated address. A withdrawal takes effect when it is received there, provided it is received at least 2 clear days before the first day of the event, counted as in rule 1.2. An effective withdrawal removes the notice from both limits.

1.7 Where the Board has passed a resolution for a named premises and calendar year, the event-day figure in rule 1.4 for that premises and year is the figure stated in the resolution.

1.8 The limits in rules 1.3 and 1.4 are applied to the calendar year in which the first event day falls.

1. PURPOSE
This note records the filing history, the adopted stock figures and the follow-up points for the annual hazardous stock declaration from Stendfell Depot for the year ended on the reporting year-end date above. Figures are those held on the file on the note date. The note does not change the procedure.

2. PROCEDURE EXTRACTS (CP-HS-3.1 rev 2)
2.1 Filing deadline: the declaration is due on the fifteenth business day after the reporting year-end. Counting starts on the day after the year-end; the year-end day itself is not counted.
2.2 Business day: a day from Monday to Friday that is not listed in the holiday schedule at 2.8. Weekends are never business days. A listed holiday is not a business day even when it falls on a weekday.
2.3 Extensions: the regulator's officer may set a later filing date for a named declaration. An extension counts only if it is in writing from the named officer and states a calendar date. An extension replaces the standard deadline for that declaration and changes no other date in this procedure. A telephone conversation with any other regulator staff member is not an extension.
2.4 Class A notice: where the adopted Class A quantity is more than 2,000 kg, a named-substance notice must accompany the declaration.
2.5 Inspection category: where the adopted total of all declared classes is under 5.0 tonnes, the site is Category 1 and is inspected within 120 days of receipt. Where the adopted total is 5.0 tonnes or more, the site is Category 2 and is inspected within 60 days of receipt.
2.6 Corrections: a stock correction entered before the declaration is received replaces the earlier figure for that class in full. A correction entered after receipt is filed as a separate amendment and does not change the declared figure.
2.7 Units: quantities are reported in kilograms. One tonne is 1,000 kg. A quantity given in tonnes is multiplied by 1,000 to give kilograms.
2.8 Holiday schedule 2026: 2026-01-01 and 2026-01-02 are non-working days at all Rijourell sites. No other dates in January 2026 are listed.
2.9 Record retention: receipts, extension letters and correction entries are kept for seven years from the reporting year-end.

visits.field_note: Window cut short by gusts; counted as recorded only.

policy.rule_text: Works that would disturb or destroy a roost must not proceed without a mitigation licence where the roost likelihood score is at or above the licence threshold. Postponing works to another season does not remove this requirement while a roost may be present.

q1.instructions: Which action should the surveyor recommend to the client before any demolition of the barn starts?

criteria.defer_to_next_season: Postpone the works to a later season without applying for any mitigation licence.
criteria.seek_mitigation_licence: Hold the works and apply for a mitigation licence before any disturbance to a possible roost.

q2.instructions: Rate the likelihood that a bat roost is present in the barn, using only the survey visits that meet the protocol's validity conditions.
criteria: Unlikely: no emergence recorded on any valid visit, and no droppings found
Possible: emergence recorded on exactly one valid visit, or droppings found with no emergence on any valid visit
Likely: emergence recorded on at least two valid visits, with no roost directly observed occupied
Near certain: a roost directly observed occupied on a valid visit

q3.instructions: The report was issued more than 28 calendar days after the last valid survey visit.

criteria.true: The issue date falls more than 28 calendar days after the date of the last visit that meets the protocol's validity conditions.
criteria.false: The issue date falls on or within 28 calendar days after the date of the last visit that meets the protocol's validity conditions.

check.q1: Policy JX-POL-09 licence threshold is 'likely'. Valid visits (wind at most 20 km/h, air at least 10 C) with emergence: 2026-07-08 (11 pipistrelles) and 2026-07-22 (4 pipistrelles); two valid visits show emergence and no roost was directly observed, so the likelihood is 'likely', which equals the threshold -> licence required before disturbance. Policy says postponing does not remove the requirement, so proceeding on the programmed date and deferring without a licence are both unlawful. Licence fee 1240 GBP and 6-week determination are weighed against 850 GBP per week of delay, but the rule leaves no lawful path without the licence -> seek_mitigation_licence.
check.q2: Visit 2026-07-08: wind 9 (at most 20), air 14.5 (at least 10) -> valid. Visit 2026-07-15: wind 26 (above 20) -> invalid, excluded. Visit 2026-07-22: wind 11, air 13.0 -> valid. Valid visits with emergence: 2 (11 and 4 pipistrelles). Direct roost observation on valid visits: none. Two valid visits with emergence and no direct observation matches 'Likely' (index 2); level 3 needs a directly observed occupied roost, which is absent -> 2.
check.q3: Last valid visit: 2026-07-22 (visit 2026-07-15 excluded, wind 26 km/h). Issue date 2026-08-19. Days from 2026-07-22 to 2026-07-31 = 9; plus 19 days in August = 28 calendar days. 28 is not more than 28 -> statement false.

rankingByTotal

requestSummary.passFailRule: A bidder failing a pass/fail compliance check is not scored or ranked.

candidateResponse.notes: Totals shown to one decimal place.

panelLog.text: Panel met at the Sosfell office; minutes filed under PNL-26-0339.

q1.instructions: Does the candidate response name the bidder that the logged scores and published weights place first?

criteria.correct_top_bidder: The bidder the response names as top-ranked has the highest recomputed weighted total among the compliant bidders.
criteria.wrong_top_bidder: The bidder the response names as top-ranked has a recomputed weighted total below another compliant bidder's.
criteria.no_top_bidder_named: The response does not name any top-ranked bidder.
criteria.other: The response's top-ranking claim fails in some other way.

q2.instructions: Rate how many of the request's listed asks the candidate response answers.
criteria: Fewer than 2 of the 4 asks answered

q3.instructions: The weights the candidate response states for the three criteria are the same as the weights published in the request.

criteria.true: Each stated weight equals the corresponding published weight.
criteria.false: At least one stated weight differs from its published weight.

q4.instructions: Which kind of correction would change the top-ranked bidder that the response reports?

criteria.recalc_reported_total: Recalculating one reported weighted total from the logged scores and published weights would reverse the top-ranked placing.
criteria.add_exclusion_note: Adding a note about the bidder that failed compliance, without changing any figure, would reverse the top-ranked placing.
criteria.no_correction_reverses_top: None of the corrections described in the other options would reverse the top-ranked placing.

q5.instructions: Rate the accuracy of the weighted totals the response reports, as the share of reported totals that match the recomputed totals to one decimal place.
criteria: At least 50% but under 100% of reported totals match

q6.instructions: The candidate response names the bidder that failed the compliance check and gives the reason for that failure.

criteria.true: The response names the bidder that failed compliance and gives the reason for the failure.
criteria.false: The response does not name the bidder that failed compliance together with the reason for the failure.

check.q1: Response ranks Grotumex Ltd first. Recompute with weights 50/30/20: Grotumex 72x0.5=36.0 + 85x0.3=25.5 + 60x0.2=12.0 = 73.5; Lepainara 78x0.5=39.0 + 70x0.3=21.0 + 80x0.2=16.0 = 76.0; Holjounham 66x0.5=33.0 + 90x0.3=27.0 + 55x0.2=11.0 = 71.0. Highest is Lepainara at 76.0; the named bidder's 73.5 is lower -> wrong_top_bidder.
check.q2: weightedTotalPerBidder: answered (totals listed). rankingByTotal: answered (ranking listed). weightsApplied: answered (weights stated). excludedBidders: not answered (no excluded bidder named). 3 of 4 asks answered -> level index 2 (3 of the 4 asks answered).
check.q3: Stated quality 50, price 25, socialValue 25; published quality 50, price 30, socialValue 20. Price 25 is not 30 -> false.
check.q4: Recalculating Grotumex's reported 77.5 from logged scores at 50/30/20 gives 73.5; Lepainara's 76.0 then exceeds it, so the top placing reverses -> recalc_reported_total holds. Adding a note about Velfamcroft Depot Ltd changes no score or total, so the top stays Grotumex Ltd -> add_exclusion_note does not hold. Because recalc_reported_total reverses the top, no_correction_reverses_top does not hold.
check.q5: Reported vs recomputed: Grotumex 77.5 vs 73.5 (no match); Lepainara 76.0 vs 76.0 (match); Holjounham 71.0 vs 71.0 (match). 2 of 3 = 66.7%, which is at least 50% and under 100% -> level index 1.
check.q6: Response totals, ranking and notes name only Grotumex Ltd, Lepainara Trust and Holjounham Fleet Ltd. Velfamcroft Depot Ltd and its compliance failure reason do not appear -> statement is false.

1. SCOPE
This file records the assessment of a temperature excursion on a refrigerated load carried on Thursday 12 March 2026. The load is batch BT-5521 (insulin pen 4-packs, pharmacy supply). It was carried in van VN-4417 from Frondgate Depot to Brithorpe Community Pharmacy, delivery drop DL-0912. The assessment is made under Procedure SOP CC-14, Revision 3, effective 1 February 2026.

2. PROCEDURE EXTRACTS (SOP CC-14 Rev 3)
4.1 Storage range for the product is 2.0°C to 8.0°C inclusive. Any logged reading above 8.0°C is an excursion reading.
4.2 Loggers record one reading every 5 minutes. Each logged excursion reading stands for 5 minutes above 8.0°C. Time is not interpolated between readings.
4.3 A run of consecutive excursion readings is one excursion block. Two blocks belong to the same event unless the logged readings between them include a run of at least 6 consecutive readings at or below 8.0°C (30 minutes or more). Where that happens the blocks are separate events. The time of an event is its number of excursion readings multiplied by 5 minutes; readings at or below 8.0°C are not counted as exposure. Separate events are assessed one at a time and their times are never added together for the test in 4.4.
4.4 Notification to the Relminster Medicines Inspectorate is required where a single event EXCEEDS the notification threshold in force for the load on the date of the event. Threshold figures are set in section 3 of this file.
4.5 Any batch with at least one excursion reading must be placed on hold pending stability review. The batch may be released only after that review, by a written release signed by the Quality Lead.

3. AMENDMENT A
Issued 2 March 2026 by Lesett Folley, Quality Lead. Effective 1 March 2026.
Rev 3 section 4.4 applied one threshold of 60 minutes to every vehicle. Amendment A replaces that with two thresholds. The test in 4.4 (the event must exceed the threshold) is unchanged.
- Load carried in a vehicle holding a current refrigeration validation certificate: threshold 90 minutes for a single event.
- Load carried in any other vehicle: threshold 60 minutes for a single event.
Amendment A does not change 4.1 to 4.3 or 4.5.

Status counts only if the contextual flag was confirmed on or before the offer issue date. The confirmation date in the coordinator log governs, whatever the offer template prints. 4.5 Results review. A regrade notified in writing by the Chair of the Results Review Panel replaces the grade on the results record from the date of that notice. A regrade notified by any other officer does not change offer status until the Chair confirms it in writing.

4.6 Deferral. A request to defer entry to the following cycle must be made in writing before 1 September of the entry year. Deferral requests are not considered from applicants who have not returned a firm acceptance.

4.7 Appeals. An appeal against an admissions decision must be lodged within 10 working days of the decision letter. Appeals go to a panel that does not include the officer who made the decision.

4.8 Accommodation. Campus accommodation allocation is administered separately and is not an offer condition.

4.9 Records. The results record is updated only from the official results release or from a regrade notice issued under 4.5.

state.notes: Door-open telemetry is stamped in UTC, while dock entries, gate entries and the yard board are in site local time. Line 4 was transferred to TRL-4472 at the gate on the same shift and appears here only for the transfer audit. The night team reapplied seal SL-88213 after the reclose was logged. The setpoint was held at the depot during dwell and sensor RF-07 was not moved between trailers. criteria.false: With both stamps on the same clock, the interval from door-open to reclose is 90 minutes or less.

criteria.under_limit_by_less_than_100kg: On-board weight is below the maximum payload by less than 100 kg.
criteria.at_or_over_limit: On-board weight equals or exceeds the maximum payload.

q3.instructions: Rate the time the trailer spent waiting at the site between gate-in and door assignment, using the terminal clock.

q4.instructions: The pallets on the lines that are on board add up to the on-board pallet count on the manifest.

criteria.false: The sum of pallets on the lines marked on board differs from the manifest's on-board pallet count.

REPORTING STANDARD RS-7, SECTION 4 (EXCERPT)
4.1 Unplanned interruptions are summed by event. An event is reportable when the summed customer-minutes lost across all unplanned interruptions recorded against that event exceed 120,000.

domain: 33 kV substation transformer outage planning

fleet_reliability.annual_probability_method: fleet failures divided by fleet transformer-years, used directly as the annual failure probability for a unit of this type

consequence.includes: replacement unit hire, emergency crew, customer compensation

state.decision_rule: Schedule a planned outage only when expected avoided loss (annual failure probability multiplied by unplanned failure cost) exceeds the planned outage cost.
state.notes: OS-1114 was taken during a cold snap; the lab reports no change in moisture trend. Fardrourica Power Ltd has asked for a copy of this review for the regional asset register. Tap changer inspection completed in 2024 with no defects noted.

q1.instructions: The planned outage is scheduled more than 90 days after the most recent oil sample was taken.

criteria.true: The calendar gap from the latest oil sample date to the scheduled outage date is more than 90 days.
criteria.false: The calendar gap from the latest oil sample date to the scheduled outage date is 90 days or fewer.

q2.instructions: Under the planning rule in the record, what course of action should the planner take for this transformer in the planned outage window?

criteria.schedule_outage_now: Take the unit out of service in the planned window for replacement or major works, because the expected avoided loss exceeds the planned outage cost.
criteria.continue_monitoring: Keep the unit in service under routine monitoring and take no planned outage in this window, because the expected avoided loss does not exceed the planned outage cost.

q3.instructions: Rate the annual likelihood of an unplanned failure of this transformer, using the planning convention stated in the record.

check.q1: Latest sample OS-1114 taken 2026-02-11; outage scheduled 2026-05-19. Feb 11 to Mar 11 = 28 days; Mar 11 to Apr 11 = 31; Apr 11 to May 11 = 30; May 11 to May 19 = 8; total 97 days, which is more than 90 -> true.
check.q2: Fleet failures 3 / transformer-years 240 = 0.0125 (1.25% annual). Expected avoided loss = 0.0125 x GBP 410,000 = GBP 5,125. Planned outage cost GBP 18,000. GBP 5,125 does not exceed GBP 18,000 -> rule not met -> continue_monitoring.
check.q3: Fleet failures 3 / transformer-years 240 = 0.0125 = 1.25% annual. Bands: under 1% remote; at least 1% but under 3% low; 1.25% falls in low -> index 1.

state:
INTERNAL MEMO
Reference: PBE-SV-0417
From: Dreacken Golhurst, Survey Coordinator, Pillbeckis Ecology Ltd
To: Brecka Kortley, Site Lead, Vesrellex Estates Ltd
Date: 14 March 2026
Subject: Dusk emergence survey results, Barn 3, Clurtbury Farm Lane, Sulport

1. Background
Barn 3 is the subject of a planning application to convert the building into two dwellings. The slate roof has lifted ridge tiles on the north side. A common pipistrelle roost is recorded about 1.2 km south of the site, outside the application boundary.

2. Survey method
Twenty dusk emergence visits were carried out between 5 May 2025 and 28 July 2025. Each visit ran the full 90-minute window from sunset, and every visit was completed. Observers stood at two fixed points and recorded whether any bat left the building. A visit is positive if an observer confirmed at least one emergence, and negative otherwise.
Detector units logged bat passes throughout each dusk visit. A pass is one bat call sequence recorded by a detector. Pass totals per visit are listed in Annex B.
Four dawn re-entry visits were made on 2 June, 16 June, 30 June and 14 July 2025. They are reported in Annex C and are not part of the dusk figures.

3. Dusk results
Positive visits: 13
Negative visits: 7
Total dusk visits: 20
Detector-logged bat passes across all dusk visits: 46

4. Likelihood rule
For the planning file, the likelihood that an occupied roost is present is taken as the share of dusk visits that were positive. Dawn re-entry results and detector pass totals do not enter that share.

5. Decision inputs supplied by the client
- Licensed mitigation plan lodged now: £7,500 fixed. If a roost is present, nothing further is payable, because the plan already covers it.
- Further survey visits over an extra season: £4,800 fixed, with a 6-week delay costing £1,500 per week. If a roost is then found, the £7,500 mitigation plan must still be lodged.
- Proceeding with works without a mitigation plan: no fixed cost. If an occupied roost is present, the penalty and remedial cost payable is £40,000.

Decision rule agreed with the client: for each option, total expected cost equals fixed fees plus delay cost, plus the likelihood of an occupied roost multiplied by the cost payable if a roost is present under that option. The option with the lowest total expected cost is preferred.

6. Other notes
Survey fee invoice PBE-INV-88213 is payable within 30 days. Queries to b.kortley@vesrellex-estates.co.uk.

criteria: Low: under 25% of dusk visits positive
Moderate: 25% to under 50% of dusk visits positive
High: 50% to under 75% of dusk visits positive
Very high: 75% or more of dusk visits positive

criteria.true: Total logged passes on the dusk visits, divided by the total dusk survey hours, is greater than 1.5.
criteria.false: Total logged passes on the dusk visits, divided by the total dusk survey hours, is 1.5 or less.

q3.instructions: Under the agreed decision rule, which course of action has the lowest total expected cost?

criteria.file_mitigation_now: Lodge the works application now with a licensed mitigation plan for the building.
criteria.commission_further_visits: Delay the application to commission extra survey visits before deciding on mitigation.
criteria.proceed_without_plan: Carry out the works without a mitigation plan.

Allowed loading laytime is 60 running hours. Laytime commences six hours after tender of a valid Notice of Readiness (NOR), whether or not the vessel has berthed. Loading laytime ends when loading is completed and hatches are closed.
Rain stoppages: a suspension of loading with hatches closed because of rain is excluded from laytime only if it lasts two or more continuous hours, and the whole stoppage is then excluded. CLALWORIS COLLEGE OF WEALBURY
Undergraduate Admissions - Decision File Printout

SECTION A - POLICY EXTRACT ADM-POL-4 (version 3.1, effective 2026-01-05)

4.1 Conditional offers. A conditional offer states the A-level grades required. Grades are read from the official results statement received by the Admissions Office. The results release date is recorded in the file header as resultsReleaseDate.

4.2 Contextual holds. Where a school context flag has been confirmed by the Widening Participation Panel, and the achieved grades fall short of the offer by exactly one grade in exactly one subject, the Admissions Office may issue a revised offer on a contextual hold. No contextual hold may be issued where the shortfall spans more than one subject or more than one grade.

4.3 Timing of panel confirmation. The Panel's confirmation must be recorded on the file on or before the results release date.

4.3(a) Exception E-2. A confirmation recorded after the results release date is treated as on time where both of the following apply: (i) the Panel had received the school's context documents on or before the results release date; and (ii) the confirmation is recorded no later than 5 working days after the results release date.

4.4 Revised offers. A revised offer must be accepted in writing within 10 working days of the revised offer date. Counting starts on the first working day after the revised offer date, and the 10th working day counted is the last day for acceptance.

4.5 Late acceptance. An acceptance received after the last day in 4.4 has lapsed. A lapsed revised offer may be reinstated only where the acceptance is received no more than 2 working days after that last day; otherwise the place is released to the waiting list. Working days after the last day are counted from the first working day after it up to and including the day of receipt.

4.6 Working days are Monday to Friday, excluding these 2026 closure days: 2026-08-31, 2026-12-25 and 2026-12-28.

rules.text: An excursion day is a calendar date on which at least one valid temperature reading for the review unit, dated that day, is above the maximum holding temperature. Each calendar date counts once, however many readings on that date are above the maximum.

A reading is voided only where a sensor fault is entered in the maintenance log for the review unit on the reading date, and a re-check reading for the review unit is taken no later than 2 calendar days after the reading date. A voided reading is disregarded for all purposes in this review, and the re-check reading stands in its place.
A correction notice replaces the reported temperature of the referenced reading with the corrected temperature stated in the notice, for all purposes in this review.
Where the number of excursion days in a review period is 3 or more, a corrective action plan must be submitted under the plan rule.
A follow-up return is due within 14 calendar days after the inspection date, unless the authority approves a later date in writing, in which case the approved date applies.
A corrective-action step is met if it is completed on or before its due date, or on or before a later date approved in writing by the authority.
Readings dated after the review period end are outside this review.

SECTION 1. PROCEDURE EXTRACT

4.1 Warm reading. A logged reading warmer than -65 °C is a warm reading. A logged reading at or colder than -65 °C is a cold reading.

4.2 Excursion episode. An episode starts at the first warm reading after a cold reading. It ends at the first cold reading after that. Its duration is the number of minutes from the start reading to the end reading. Warm readings that follow one another belong to the same episode.

4.3 Daily allowance. Episode durations are added together by the calendar date of the episode start reading, counting 00:00 to 23:59 on that date. The daily allowance is the total episode time permitted for a freezer on that date. Where the total for a date is more than the daily allowance in force on that date, all samples held in that freezer are placed in quarantine pending QA review.

4.4 Single-episode trigger. Any single episode longer than 20 minutes requires a written deviation note, whatever the daily total. A deviation note and quarantine can both apply to the same event.

4.5 Alarms and acknowledgment. The logger raises an alarm at the start reading of each episode. Silencing the audible alarm at the unit is not an acknowledgment. An alarm is acknowledged only when an entry is made on the logger system.

4.6 Escalation. If an alarm is not acknowledged on the logger system within 15 minutes of its start reading, the logger sends an escalation message to the on-call technician at the 15-minute point. A later acknowledgment does not cancel an escalation already sent.

4.7 Allowance set by QA. The daily allowance for each freezer is 60 minutes unless QA has issued a written reduction for that freezer. A reduction applies only from the effective date stated in the latest written notice on file for that freezer.

4.8 Times and records. Start, end, acknowledgment and escalation times are read from the logger record, which governs event times. The latest QA notice on file governs the allowance.

4.9 Door access during an episode. Staff must not open the freezer door during an episode except to move samples to backup unit UF-12. Each door opening is written on the cold store access sheet with the time and the sample box numbers.
